title: Late-expiration summary spirometry adds negligible wheeze classification beyond duration and standard indices in two NHANES samples
abstract: In NHANES adults aged20–79 with reproducible spirometry and expiration>=6seconds, we tested summary 1−FEV6/FVC for past-year wheeze beyond flexible FEV1,FVC,FEV1/FVC,PEF,FEF25–75,forced expiratory time,demographics and smoking. Development2007–08 included3647 adults; independent-sample confirmation2009–10 included4092. Discovery PSU-grouped cross-validation Brier gain was−0.000112796. Frozen confirmation gain was+0.00000299033; target-only95% interval+0.00000043553 to+0.00000546131, but source/target refits gave−0.000383298 to+0.000471525. Removing duration increased gain to0.000340775. Linear and FEV3-adjusted baselines reversed the sign. The tiny conditional gain does not establish stable incremental value or clinical utility. Summary variables may originate from different blows; this is not a measured same-maneuver tail fraction. Confirmation is within the same survey program,not external-program validation. Author checks and clean offline rerun are supplied,not independent peer review.
